notes.claim: A power's index says how many times the base is multiplied by itself, and the index laws apply when the bases are the same.
Fractional exponents are defined as roots, which makes sense from the rule for powers of powers.
A prefix on a unit symbol forms one new symbol that can be raised to a power, and milli is the prefix for one thousandth, 10⁻³.

sources.title: Using an index or power - Laws of indices - AQA - GCSE Maths Revision - AQA - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: The power or index shows how many times a number has been multiplied by itself.

sources.title: Laws of indices for multiplication and division - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: The base numbers are the same (9), so add the indices together (3 + 5 = 8). 9³ x 9⁵ = 9⁸

sources.title: Radicals (Roots) and Fractional Exponents - UM Math Prep — University of Michigan
sources.quote: Fractional exponents are defined as roots, which makes sense from the rule for powers of powers

sources.title: Milli- - Wikipedia
sources.quote: Milli (symbol m ) is a unit prefix in the metric system denoting a factor of one thousandth (10 −3 ).

sources.title: NIST Guide to the SI, Chapter 6: Rules and Style Conventions for Printing and Using Units | NIST
sources.quote: The grouping formed by a prefix symbol attached to a unit symbol constitutes a new inseparable symbol (forming a multiple or submultiple of the unit concerned) which can be raised to a positive or negative power
